newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Higher oil price fuels BP profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Higher oil price fuels BP profit.

text.p: British Petroleum (BP) on Tuesday reported a 30 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 2.62 billion pounds ($4.28 billion), thanks to productivity gains and strong oil prices.
The result excludes a fourth quarter exceptional charge of 341 million pounds covering one-off costs related to the merger of BP and Mobil Corp's downstream operations in Europe.

The company said productivity improvements through volume growth, higher value sales and cost reductions produced gains of around $600 million, generating most of the year-on-year improvement in underlying profit.
Although oil prices were higher, particularly during the second half of the year, BP said this benefit was partly offset by lower chemical margins.
BP said "targets are in place to keep underlying performance improving", adding there may be some oil price volatilty in coming months because of worldwide production growth.

The company said continuing strong demand, relatively modest production increases and the decision by the Organisation of Oil Producing Countries (OPEC) in December to roll over its production quotas enabled the oil market to absorb the initial resumption in oil exports from Iraq.
But it said an increase in the rate of production growth over the coming months might subject oil prices to renewed volatility.
BP said it expects its own oil production to increase further this year, while pressure on refined oil products margins may moderate if the crude oil price weakens during the year.
Refining margins are likely to remain subdued with some volatility seen over the winter months due to low gasoil stock levels.
In chemicals, healthy demand should keep prices steady, but margins may continue to be affected by bigh oil-related feedstock prices. Results will remain sensitive to the pound's strength, BP said.

Net profits before exceptional items rose by 27 percent in the fourth quarter to 689 million pounds, and the company raised its quarterly dividend by five percent over the previous quarter to 5.25 pence, making for a 28 percent rise in total dividend for the year of 19.5 pence.

The results compared with market forecasts of between 2.5 and 2.75 billion pounds for the year. BP shares fell after the results, however, touching a low of 695 pence before moving back up to 702p by 1345 GMT, a loss of 19 pence on the day.
BP increased capital expenditure by 21 percent to 3.44 billion pounds in the year, while the net cash inflow was 314 million pounds.

BP's exploration and production division made fourth quarter figures of 814 million pounds, 41 percent ahead of a year earlier due to stronger oil prices, higher production and continued containment of costs.
Refining and marketing increased underlying profits by 98 million pounds to 163 million due to improved refinery performance, marketing sales and lower costs.
But the result from chemicals was down by 26 million pounds on the previous quarter to 104 million due to the effect of higher naphtha feedstock prices and the strength of sterling. ($1=.6120 Pound)
